q: What is the correct definition of Scarcity?
o: Unemployment from mismatch of skills or locations
Limited resources relative to unlimited wants
Difference between willingness to pay and actual price
Average tax rate rises as income rises
e: Scarcity: Limited resources relative to unlimited wants. Makes choices and trade-offs necessary

q: What is the correct definition of Opportunity cost?
o: Tax imposed on imported goods
Market with a single dominant seller and high barriers to entry
Unemployment caused by economic downturns
Value of the next best alternative forgone
e: Opportunity cost: Value of the next best alternative forgone. Relevant cost of a choice

q: What is the correct definition of Production possibility frontier?
o: Increase in the stock of productive assets
Share of the labour force without work but seeking and available for work
Curve showing maximum feasible output combinations
High inflation combined with weak growth and high unemployment
e: Production possibility frontier: Curve showing maximum feasible output combinations. Points inside indicate underused resources

q: What is the correct definition of Demand?
o: Official reduction in a fixed exchange rate
Output produced per unit of input
Total output firms are willing to produce at different price levels
Quantity consumers are willing and able to buy at different prices
e: Demand: Quantity consumers are willing and able to buy at different prices. Usually slopes downward, other things equal

q: What is the correct definition of Supply?
o: Limited resources relative to unlimited wants
Quantity producers are willing and able to sell at different prices
Skills, knowledge and health embodied in people
Record of transactions between residents and the rest of the world
e: Supply: Quantity producers are willing and able to sell at different prices. Usually slopes upward, other things equal

q: What is the correct definition of Market equilibrium?
o: Price and quantity where demand equals supply
Stock of money available in an economy
Broader improvement in welfare, institutions and productive capacity
Ability to produce at lower opportunity cost
e: Market equilibrium: Price and quantity where demand equals supply. No tendency for price to change absent shocks

q: What is the correct definition of Price elasticity of demand?
o: Increase in the stock of productive assets
Increase in an economy's real output over time
Responsiveness of quantity demanded to a price change
Significant decline in economic activity across the economy
e: Price elasticity of demand: Responsiveness of quantity demanded to a price change. Elasticity greater than one is elastic

q: What is the correct definition of Income elasticity of demand?
o: Price and quantity where demand equals supply
Responsiveness of demand to income change
Income earned by a country's residents including net income from abroad
Composite index of health, education and income
e: Income elasticity of demand: Responsiveness of demand to income change. Can distinguish normal and inferior goods

q: What is the correct definition of Cross-price elasticity?
o: Balance covering goods, services, primary income and transfers
Price of one currency in terms of another
Responsiveness of demand for one good to another good's price
Market dominated by a small number of firms
e: Cross-price elasticity: Responsiveness of demand for one good to another good's price. Positive for substitutes and negative for complements

q: What is the correct definition of Consumer surplus?
o: Short-term unemployment during job search and transitions
Ratio of total income change to an initial autonomous spending change
Share of an additional unit of income spent on consumption
Difference between willingness to pay and actual price
e: Consumer surplus: Difference between willingness to pay and actual price. Measures buyer benefit

q: What is the correct definition of Producer surplus?
o: Share of the labour force without work but seeking and available for work
Difference between market price and minimum acceptable price
Ability to produce at lower opportunity cost
Income earned by a country's residents including net income from abroad
e: Producer surplus: Difference between market price and minimum acceptable price. Measures seller benefit

q: What is the correct definition of Externality?
o: Record of transactions between residents and the rest of the world
Cost or benefit imposed on a third party
Ratio of total income change to an initial autonomous spending change
Price of one currency in terms of another
e: Externality: Cost or benefit imposed on a third party. Can be positive or negative

q: What is the correct definition of Public good?
o: Good that is non-rival and non-excludable
Composite index of health, education and income
Government spending exceeds revenue in a period
Share of an additional unit of income spent on consumption
e: Public good: Good that is non-rival and non-excludable. National defence is a common example

q: What is the correct definition of Common-pool resource?
o: Resource that is rival but difficult to exclude users from
GDP adjusted for changes in the price level
Graph showing cumulative distribution of income or wealth
Quantitative limit on imports or exports
e: Common-pool resource: Resource that is rival but difficult to exclude users from. Can face overuse

q: What is the correct definition of Monopoly?
o: Development meeting present needs without undermining future generations
Income earned by a country's residents including net income from abroad
Sustained decrease in the general price level
Market with a single dominant seller and high barriers to entry
e: Monopoly: Market with a single dominant seller and high barriers to entry. Possesses market power

q: What is the correct definition of Oligopoly?
o: Unemployment caused by economic downturns
Income earned by a country's residents including net income from abroad
Market dominated by a small number of firms
Balance covering goods, services, primary income and transfers
e: Oligopoly: Market dominated by a small number of firms. Strategic interdependence is important

q: What is the correct definition of Perfect competition?
o: Index tracking prices of a representative consumer basket
Unemployment from mismatch of skills or locations
Market with many firms, homogeneous products and free entry
Graph showing cumulative distribution of income or wealth
e: Perfect competition: Market with many firms, homogeneous products and free entry. Individual firms are price takers

q: What is the correct definition of Monopolistic competition?
o: Graph showing cumulative distribution of income or wealth
Market with many firms selling differentiated products
Good that is non-rival and non-excludable
Limited resources relative to unlimited wants
e: Monopolistic competition: Market with many firms selling differentiated products. Firms have some pricing power

q: What is the correct definition of Gross domestic product?
o: Responsiveness of demand for one good to another good's price
Index tracking prices of a representative consumer basket
Market value of final goods and services produced within a country
Share of the labour force without work but seeking and available for work
e: Gross domestic product: Market value of final goods and services produced within a country. Measures domestic production

q: What is the correct definition of Gross national income?
o: Market value of final goods and services produced within a country
Income earned by a country's residents including net income from abroad
Responsiveness of demand to income change
Increase in an economy's real output over time
e: Gross national income: Income earned by a country's residents including net income from abroad. Focuses on residents rather than location of production

q: What is the correct definition of Nominal GDP?
o: Total output firms are willing to produce at different price levels
Exceptionally severe and prolonged economic downturn
GDP measured at current prices
Ratio of total income change to an initial autonomous spending change
e: Nominal GDP: GDP measured at current prices. Affected by price changes

q: What is the correct definition of Real GDP?
o: Total output firms are willing to produce at different price levels
Share of an additional unit of income spent on consumption
GDP adjusted for changes in the price level
Market value of final goods and services produced within a country
e: Real GDP: GDP adjusted for changes in the price level. Used to measure output growth

q: What is the correct definition of GDP deflator?
o: Increase in an economy's real output over time
Total planned spending on domestic output
Broad price index derived from nominal and real GDP
Difference between market price and minimum acceptable price
e: GDP deflator: Broad price index derived from nominal and real GDP. Covers domestically produced final output

q: What is the correct definition of Inflation?
o: Decline in the rate of inflation
Tax imposed on imported goods
Sustained increase in the general price level
Cross-border purchase of financial assets without managerial control
e: Inflation: Sustained increase in the general price level. Reduces purchasing power of money

q: What is the correct definition of Deflation?
o: Sustained decrease in the general price level
Outstanding liabilities of government
Fall in a currency's value under a floating exchange-rate system
Ability to produce at lower opportunity cost
e: Deflation: Sustained decrease in the general price level. Can increase real burden of debt

q: What is the correct definition of Disinflation?
o: Skills, knowledge and health embodied in people
Decline in the rate of inflation
Measure of inequality ranging conventionally from zero to one
Development meeting present needs without undermining future generations
e: Disinflation: Decline in the rate of inflation. Prices may still be rising more slowly

q: What is the correct definition of Consumer price index?
o: Index tracking prices of a representative consumer basket
Curve showing maximum feasible output combinations
Market with many firms selling differentiated products
Responsiveness of demand to income change
e: Consumer price index: Index tracking prices of a representative consumer basket. Common measure of cost-of-living changes

q: What is the correct definition of Unemployment rate?
o: Market with a single dominant seller and high barriers to entry
Responsiveness of quantity demanded to a price change
Share of the labour force without work but seeking and available for work
Sustained decrease in the general price level
e: Unemployment rate: Share of the labour force without work but seeking and available for work. Excludes people outside the labour force

q: What is the correct definition of Frictional unemployment?
o: Fall in a currency's value under a floating exchange-rate system
Cost or benefit imposed on a third party
Short-term unemployment during job search and transitions
Imports of goods and services exceed exports
e: Frictional unemployment: Short-term unemployment during job search and transitions. Exists even in healthy labour markets

q: What is the correct definition of Structural unemployment?
o: Unemployment from mismatch of skills or locations
Unemployment caused by economic downturns
Difference between willingness to pay and actual price
Measure of inequality ranging conventionally from zero to one
e: Structural unemployment: Unemployment from mismatch of skills or locations. Can persist despite vacancies

q: What is the correct definition of Cyclical unemployment?
o: Unemployment caused by economic downturns
Value of the next best alternative forgone
Tax imposed directly on income or wealth
Stock of money available in an economy
e: Cyclical unemployment: Unemployment caused by economic downturns. Rises during recessions

q: What is the correct definition of Fiscal policy?
o: Tax imposed on imported goods
Development meeting present needs without undermining future generations
Government use of spending and taxation to influence the economy
Responsiveness of demand to income change
e: Fiscal policy: Government use of spending and taxation to influence the economy. Can be expansionary or contractionary

q: What is the correct definition of Monetary policy?
o: Curve showing maximum feasible output combinations
Central-bank management of money and interest-rate conditions
Fall in a currency's value under a floating exchange-rate system
Minimum reserves banks must hold against deposits
e: Monetary policy: Central-bank management of money and interest-rate conditions. Aims commonly include price stability

q: What is the correct definition of Policy interest rate?
o: Tax imposed on transactions or goods and services
Central-bank purchases or sales of securities
Fall in a currency's value under a floating exchange-rate system
Benchmark rate set or targeted by a central bank
e: Policy interest rate: Benchmark rate set or targeted by a central bank. Influences borrowing conditions

q: What is the correct definition of Open market operations?
o: Share of the labour force without work but seeking and available for work
Market with many firms, homogeneous products and free entry
Record of transactions between residents and the rest of the world
Central-bank purchases or sales of securities
e: Open market operations: Central-bank purchases or sales of securities. Used to manage liquidity and interest rates

q: What is the correct definition of Reserve requirement?
o: Official reduction in a fixed exchange rate
Unemployment from mismatch of skills or locations
Share of an additional unit of income spent on consumption
Minimum reserves banks must hold against deposits
e: Reserve requirement: Minimum reserves banks must hold against deposits. Affects money creation

q: What is the correct definition of Money supply?
o: Short-term unemployment during job search and transitions
Stock of money available in an economy
Increase in the stock of productive assets
Index tracking prices of a representative consumer basket
e: Money supply: Stock of money available in an economy. Measured through aggregates such as M1 and M2

q: What is the correct definition of Liquidity?
o: Balance covering goods, services, primary income and transfers
Tax imposed on imported goods
Income or consumption threshold used to identify poverty
Ease with which an asset can be converted into cash without major loss
e: Liquidity: Ease with which an asset can be converted into cash without major loss. Cash is highly liquid

q: What is the correct definition of Exchange rate?
o: Price of one currency in terms of another
Difference between market price and minimum acceptable price
Development meeting present needs without undermining future generations
Sustained increase in the general price level
e: Exchange rate: Price of one currency in terms of another. Can float or be managed

q: What is the correct definition of Currency depreciation?
o: Difference between willingness to pay and actual price
Fall in a currency's value under a floating exchange-rate system
Composite index of health, education and income
GDP measured at current prices
e: Currency depreciation: Fall in a currency's value under a floating exchange-rate system. Makes imports more expensive, other things equal

q: What is the correct definition of Currency devaluation?
o: Official reduction in a fixed exchange rate
Record of transactions between residents and the rest of the world
Broader improvement in welfare, institutions and productive capacity
Minimum reserves banks must hold against deposits
e: Currency devaluation: Official reduction in a fixed exchange rate. Policy action under a pegged regime

q: What is the correct definition of Balance of payments?
o: Cross-border investment involving lasting control or influence
Record of transactions between residents and the rest of the world
Average tax rate rises as income rises
Decline in the rate of inflation
e: Balance of payments: Record of transactions between residents and the rest of the world. Includes current and financial accounts

q: What is the correct definition of Current account?
o: Tax imposed on imported goods
Index tracking prices of a representative consumer basket
Spending on capital goods or additions to inventories
Balance covering goods, services, primary income and transfers
e: Current account: Balance covering goods, services, primary income and transfers. Part of the balance of payments

q: What is the correct definition of Trade deficit?
o: Imports of goods and services exceed exports
Resource that is rival but difficult to exclude users from
Outstanding liabilities of government
Benchmark rate set or targeted by a central bank
e: Trade deficit: Imports of goods and services exceed exports. A component of the current account

q: What is the correct definition of Comparative advantage?
o: Market value of final goods and services produced within a country
Ability to produce at lower opportunity cost
GDP adjusted for changes in the price level
Government spending exceeds revenue in a period
e: Comparative advantage: Ability to produce at lower opportunity cost. Explains gains from specialization

q: What is the correct definition of Absolute advantage?
o: Price and quantity where demand equals supply
Ability to produce more with given resources
GDP measured at current prices
Increase in the stock of productive assets
e: Absolute advantage: Ability to produce more with given resources. Does not alone determine trade patterns

q: What is the correct definition of Tariff?
o: Average tax rate rises as income rises
Tax imposed on imported goods
Value of the next best alternative forgone
Ability to produce more with given resources
e: Tariff: Tax imposed on imported goods. Raises domestic price of imports

q: What is the correct definition of Quota?
o: Market with a single dominant seller and high barriers to entry
Sustained decrease in the general price level
Quantitative limit on imports or exports
Measure of inequality ranging conventionally from zero to one
e: Quota: Quantitative limit on imports or exports. Creates scarcity rents

q: What is the correct definition of Foreign direct investment?
o: Responsiveness of demand to income change
Cross-border investment involving lasting control or influence
Tax imposed on imported goods
Government payment or support lowering costs or prices
e: Foreign direct investment: Cross-border investment involving lasting control or influence. Includes greenfield investment and acquisitions

q: What is the correct definition of Portfolio investment?
o: Decline in the rate of inflation
High inflation combined with weak growth and high unemployment
Share of the labour force without work but seeking and available for work
Cross-border purchase of financial assets without managerial control
e: Portfolio investment: Cross-border purchase of financial assets without managerial control. Usually more liquid than direct investment

q: What is the correct definition of Budget deficit?
o: Tax imposed on transactions or goods and services
Total output firms are willing to produce at different price levels
High inflation combined with weak growth and high unemployment
Government spending exceeds revenue in a period
e: Budget deficit: Government spending exceeds revenue in a period. Financed through borrowing or money creation

q: What is the correct definition of Public debt?
o: Outstanding liabilities of government
Tax imposed on imported goods
Official reduction in a fixed exchange rate
Tax imposed directly on income or wealth
e: Public debt: Outstanding liabilities of government. Can be domestic or external

q: What is the correct definition of Progressive tax?
o: Average tax rate rises as income rises
Minimum reserves banks must hold against deposits
Tax imposed directly on income or wealth
Central-bank management of money and interest-rate conditions
e: Progressive tax: Average tax rate rises as income rises. Used to increase vertical equity

q: What is the correct definition of Regressive tax?
o: Broad price index derived from nominal and real GDP
Sustained decrease in the general price level
Average tax burden falls as income rises
Cross-border purchase of financial assets without managerial control
e: Regressive tax: Average tax burden falls as income rises. Consumption taxes may have regressive effects

q: What is the correct definition of Direct tax?
o: Value of the next best alternative forgone
Quantity producers are willing and able to sell at different prices
Tax imposed directly on income or wealth
Income or consumption threshold used to identify poverty
e: Direct tax: Tax imposed directly on income or wealth. Income tax is a common example

q: What is the correct definition of Indirect tax?
o: Quantity consumers are willing and able to buy at different prices
Record of transactions between residents and the rest of the world
Responsiveness of demand for one good to another good's price
Tax imposed on transactions or goods and services
e: Indirect tax: Tax imposed on transactions or goods and services. Sales tax is a common example

q: What is the correct definition of Subsidy?
o: Tax imposed on imported goods
Market with a single dominant seller and high barriers to entry
Government payment or support lowering costs or prices
Increase in the stock of productive assets
e: Subsidy: Government payment or support lowering costs or prices. Can correct externalities or distort markets

q: What is the correct definition of Poverty line?
o: Government payment or support lowering costs or prices
Unemployment caused by economic downturns
Income or consumption threshold used to identify poverty
Responsiveness of demand for one good to another good's price
e: Poverty line: Income or consumption threshold used to identify poverty. Can be national or international

q: What is the correct definition of Human capital?
o: Official reduction in a fixed exchange rate
Significant decline in economic activity across the economy
Cross-border purchase of financial assets without managerial control
Skills, knowledge and health embodied in people
e: Human capital: Skills, knowledge and health embodied in people. Education and health are key investments

q: What is the correct definition of Human Development Index?
o: Composite index of health, education and income
Spending on capital goods or additions to inventories
Benchmark rate set or targeted by a central bank
Exceptionally severe and prolonged economic downturn
e: Human Development Index: Composite index of health, education and income. Published by UNDP

q: What is the correct definition of Gini coefficient?
o: Ease with which an asset can be converted into cash without major loss
Measure of inequality ranging conventionally from zero to one
Difference between market price and minimum acceptable price
Skills, knowledge and health embodied in people
e: Gini coefficient: Measure of inequality ranging conventionally from zero to one. Higher values indicate greater inequality

q: What is the correct definition of Lorenz curve?
o: Central-bank purchases or sales of securities
Resource that is rival but difficult to exclude users from
Responsiveness of demand for one good to another good's price
Graph showing cumulative distribution of income or wealth
e: Lorenz curve: Graph showing cumulative distribution of income or wealth. Used to visualize inequality

q: What is the correct definition of Sustainable development?
o: Benchmark rate set or targeted by a central bank
Central-bank purchases or sales of securities
Development meeting present needs without undermining future generations
Resource that is rival but difficult to exclude users from
e: Sustainable development: Development meeting present needs without undermining future generations. Combines economic, social and environmental dimensions

q: What is the correct definition of Economic growth?
o: Composite index of health, education and income
Benchmark rate set or targeted by a central bank
Increase in an economy's real output over time
Difference between willingness to pay and actual price
e: Economic growth: Increase in an economy's real output over time. Often measured by real GDP growth

q: What is the correct definition of Economic development?
o: Broader improvement in welfare, institutions and productive capacity
Unemployment from mismatch of skills or locations
Short-term unemployment during job search and transitions
Significant decline in economic activity across the economy
e: Economic development: Broader improvement in welfare, institutions and productive capacity. More comprehensive than output growth

q: What is the correct definition of Recession?
o: Resource that is rival but difficult to exclude users from
Unemployment caused by economic downturns
Balance covering goods, services, primary income and transfers
Significant decline in economic activity across the economy
e: Recession: Significant decline in economic activity across the economy. Often associated with falling output and employment

q: What is the correct definition of Depression?
o: Broader improvement in welfare, institutions and productive capacity
Government payment or support lowering costs or prices
Skills, knowledge and health embodied in people
Exceptionally severe and prolonged economic downturn
e: Depression: Exceptionally severe and prolonged economic downturn. More serious than a typical recession

q: What is the correct definition of Stagflation?
o: High inflation combined with weak growth and high unemployment
Cost or benefit imposed on a third party
Balance covering goods, services, primary income and transfers
Ratio of total income change to an initial autonomous spending change
e: Stagflation: High inflation combined with weak growth and high unemployment. Challenges standard demand-management policy

q: What is the correct definition of Productivity?
o: Quantitative limit on imports or exports
Total output firms are willing to produce at different price levels
Development meeting present needs without undermining future generations
Output produced per unit of input
e: Productivity: Output produced per unit of input. Central to long-run living standards

q: What is the correct definition of Capital formation?
o: Increase in the stock of productive assets
Value of the next best alternative forgone
Ability to produce more with given resources
GDP adjusted for changes in the price level
e: Capital formation: Increase in the stock of productive assets. Financed by saving and investment

q: What is the correct definition of Savings?
o: Responsiveness of demand for one good to another good's price
Market with a single dominant seller and high barriers to entry
Income not used for current consumption
Market value of final goods and services produced within a country
e: Savings: Income not used for current consumption. Can finance investment

q: What is the correct definition of Investment?
o: Share of the labour force without work but seeking and available for work
Record of transactions between residents and the rest of the world
Ability to produce at lower opportunity cost
Spending on capital goods or additions to inventories
e: Investment: Spending on capital goods or additions to inventories. A component of aggregate demand

q: What is the correct definition of Multiplier?
o: Price of one currency in terms of another
Spending on capital goods or additions to inventories
Responsiveness of demand to income change
Ratio of total income change to an initial autonomous spending change
e: Multiplier: Ratio of total income change to an initial autonomous spending change. Depends partly on marginal propensity to consume

q: What is the correct definition of Marginal propensity to consume?
o: Share of an additional unit of income spent on consumption
Composite index of health, education and income
Fall in a currency's value under a floating exchange-rate system
Tax imposed on imported goods
e: Marginal propensity to consume: Share of an additional unit of income spent on consumption. Between zero and one in simple models

q: What is the correct definition of Aggregate demand?
o: Price of one currency in terms of another
High inflation combined with weak growth and high unemployment
Ease with which an asset can be converted into cash without major loss
Total planned spending on domestic output
e: Aggregate demand: Total planned spending on domestic output. Comprises consumption, investment, government spending and net exports

q: What is the correct definition of Aggregate supply?
o: Cross-border investment involving lasting control or influence
Total output firms are willing to produce at different price levels
GDP measured at current prices
Average tax rate rises as income rises
e: Aggregate supply: Total output firms are willing to produce at different price levels. Can be short-run or long-run
